MD38 / AGENT RECONSTRUCTION AND EXTENSION
Agent reconstruction and extension
Reconstruct behavior, not an imagined memory

A useful agent handoff contains enough explicit contracts for another engineer to continue without pretending to remember an earlier conversation. It names the baseline, files, space conventions, ownership, experiments and unresolved gaps. It does not claim a perfect mental replica or universal accuracy. This chapter provides such a contract for the integrated room, renderer and interaction layer; detailed console and companion anatomy remains the responsibility of their dedicated factory chapters.

The canonical evidence baseline is 1e4ef518d6943ab1af39cef3b4d558f209a17891 in Zanark/BowserBoy. Runtime dependency evidence is the explicit Three.js 0.186.1 declaration (package.json:7–9). A later repository checkout or current online manual can differ. Always distinguish “observed at the baseline” from “recommended for a new extension.”
Figure MD38.1. A reconstruction is a chain of explicit receipts, not an appeal to hidden conversation memory.
The reusable assignment

The following instructions are intended to be copied as an assignment, with writable paths and execution permissions filled in by the requesting owner. They do not grant publication, tracking synchronization or application-edit permission by themselves.
Establish scope and read before editing

Record the requested output, exact baseline and allowed write paths. Inspect the worktree without resetting unrelated changes. Preserve historical images, existing books and concurrent work. Do not inspect private ROMs, conversations, credentials or unrelated personal context. Report missing public evidence rather than searching private stores to fill a documentation gap.

Read complete src/lighting.js, src/scene.js and src/lcd-crt.js. Read relevant controller, preferences, motion, clearance and asset sections before describing their behavior. Trace actual callers and state transitions where source evidence permits; do not invent a code graph for a repository without one. Read tests as specifications and mark any skipped coverage. Public architecture is a useful orientation, not a substitute for the implementation (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:43–146).
Rebuild the world in dependency order

First establish Y zero as tabletop support. Construct the tabletop, rear wall and lower floor with the source dimensions and separate top/edge material ownership. Add the tripod body at (-13.5,0,2) with child scale 1/.017. Draw one extruded leg and share it three times around Y; add support, open drum, rims and diffuser. Preserve double-sided fabric and the explicit non-casting overrides.

Add the spotlight, two local area emitters and world-owned tabletop bounce. Do not invent a tall central pole, mechanical switch or extra room props. The actual switch model is surface metadata plus scene/UI dispatch (src/lighting.js:9–110). Attach existing console and companion factories through their returned roots and named references; do not reconstruct their detailed anatomy in the integration module.
Preserve image and light ownership

Use sRGB output and the authored tone mapping. Keep active displays basic and non-tone-mapped, but preserve the actual distinction between DS nearest-filter native canvases and GBA linear- filter canvases. Keep powered-off glass reflective. Do not treat drawLcdCrt as a native emulator shader implementation (src/scene.js:1106–1160, src/ds-controller.js:415–435).

Sample screen emission in linear space using the 24-by-16 average, bounded sampling cadence and elapsed-time smoothing. Include both companions in exposure decisions and obstacle inventory. Never call a fixture LCD-only unless tripod, room, Pear and axolotl conditions are explicitly controlled.
Preserve interaction and scheduling

Convert pointer coordinates through the canvas CSS rectangle. Respect dispatch priority, pointer capture, grab offsets, cancellation and release. For lower DS touch, raycast the whole model and accept only a nearest lower- LCD hit. Update camera/model matrices and DOM control projection before waiting for a GPU paint (src/ds-controller.js:490–514, src/scene.js:484–500).

Separate callback updates, native screen copies, room submission and fence completion. Retain resolution, threshold boundaries and bounded recovery; start new real-time experiments from current performance.now(), not stale render timestamps. Keep required fall/bounce/rise poses until presentation acknowledgment. Do not label this as full rigid-body physics.
Research and evidence instructions

Consult three to five official references for concepts that extend beyond source. For this part the checked references are Three.js color management, physical materials, shadows and cleanup, plus MDN WebGL best practices. Record URL, consultation date, supported claim and scope. Current documentation is guidance, not pinned-runtime proof. Never send local code to public search.

Maintain four evidence labels: actual implementation, documented historical observation, researched recommendation and proposed extension. For history, inspect scoped diffs and say which mechanism changed. An old test receipt does not validate a new source revision. For a new experiment, record assumptions, changed condition, fixed variables, expected outcome and the observation that would falsify the explanation.

The scene's cleanup is a useful baseline, not a universal resource tracker. If adding texture slots or shared resources, define their owner and disposal path explicitly (src/scene.js:1430–1450). The checked current cleanup guide supports unique-resource tracking, while MDN best practices supports avoiding unnecessary blocking and releasing GPU resources eagerly.
Figure MD38.2. Extension work ends at its authorized boundary; successful technical checks do not automatically authorize synchronization or publication.
Deliver a self-contained reconstruction packet

The final packet should let another agent find every necessary public source without guessing. Include a model inventory mapping components to source symbols, chapters and relevant tests. Record absent components explicitly: there is no modeled mechanical lamp switch or separate tall pole to hunt for. Include research receipts with supported concepts and historical receipts with checked changes. List what remains unverified, especially render execution, parked browser coverage and owner acceptance.

For a proposed extension, add a dependency table with changed input, owner, invalidated cache and retained invariant. A wider shade changes geometry and bounds; its material brightness need not change. A new light changes exposure-state logic and reflections; its decorative mesh need not be an obstacle unless the model actually occupies space. Such a table prevents a successor from mistaking all visible properties for one undifferentiated “appearance” setting.

Include runnable arithmetic or clearly labeled pseudocode with assumptions and expected outcomes, not fragments that reference imaginary application APIs. State whether a recipe was executed. When commands are authorized, retain exit status and exact run identity. When they are prohibited, stop at manuscript validation and say so. A complete handoff is not one that claims everything is done; it is one that makes the next permitted action and remaining evidence gap unambiguous.
MD38-W01 Specify a larger shade extension completely

Suppose the owner requests a ten-percent wider shade while preserving height and leg footprint. Compute radius .09*1.1=.099 and diameter .198/.017=11.6471 world units. The original diameter was 10.5882, so the increase is 1.0588 world units across the drum. Keep center Y .225, height .15 and rim Y values .15 and .30.

The rim's original radius .0895 is .0005 inside the drum radius. Preserving that radial inset gives new radius .0985, not .0895. Retain the tube radius unless a thicker seam is separately requested. Check the transmitted rectangle at X .11 against the wider fabric: the source's anti-seam offset deserves renewed inspection, not automatic rescaling.
This runnable Node recipe calculates proposed dimensions only. It does not modify any model or claim the enlarged shade is accepted.

The implementation plan must include new geometry creation, old owned geometry disposal, lamp-bound recomputation, clearance with all companions, main-view invalidation and reflection refresh. Acceptance should include fixed leg footprint, unchanged light switches, no invented pole, no seam and unchanged active LCD colors. Human review decides whether the wider shade is preferable.

Keep calculated values unrounded in code and round only their displayed explanation. The diameter increase is exactly .018/.017 world units under these assumptions. Independently rounding old and new diameters before subtraction can produce a different last printed digit. This
small example mirrors the clearance algorithm's larger lesson: numerical presentation is not authoritative simulation state.
MD38-R01 Retry when the new bounds block the desk

Change the condition: the widened shade's world bounds leave no legal table layout under current priorities. First verify that the bounds include actual geometry and were not enlarged twice by metric conversion. If the bound is correct, do not move the fixed tripod silently.

The resolver must stage both equal-ranked console orders with stable tie behavior, then report failure if neither works (src/scene.js:849–890). Offer an explicitly proposed alternative, such as a smaller diameter or a separately authorized world placement change. Preserve saved poses and rollback semantics. If the application regression repeats after one bounded repair, retain the assertions and park coverage debt rather than shrinking gaps until it passes.
MD38-Q01 Exercise: write the final handoff

The agent has written the extension and run only unit tests. Browser startup failed twice, images have not been reviewed, and publication was not authorized. What should the final message contain, and what must it not imply?
MD38-A01 Explained answer

Report exact changed files, baseline, computed dimensions, commands actually executed, unit outcomes and browser failure receipts. State the bounded repair attempted, retained assertions, parked scenario and issue/Project update needed from the authorized owner. Mark visual and aesthetic review pending. Say explicitly that no deployment occurred.

Use the real eight-field numbered workstream and causal ledger practice when authorized. Preview synchronization, read the actual issue backlink rather than guessing its number, and verify remote state after any approved apply (docs/GITHUB-TRACKING.md:1–63). That process still grants no implicit publishing permission.

Finally preserve the public presentation: the root README remains GIF-first, and standalone books provide detailed teaching (README.md:1–30). Do not replace an inviting entry point with exhaustive validation logs. A truthful handoff makes the next action clear without claiming tests, approval, memory continuity or publication that did not occur.
The standalone agent handoff

This appendix is an execution contract for an agent that did not participate in BowserBOY's original development. Read it with the relevant model chapters and the source register. It is designed to preserve reasoning boundaries and reproducible techniques, not to impersonate an earlier assistant or assert access to its hidden reasoning.
Establish authority and the baseline

Begin by stating the requested visible outcome in ordinary language. Examples include making a facial feature travel farther without entering the body, making a hinged lid preserve its relationship to the lower deck, or making a moved lamp illuminate the scene from its new position. Keep the outcome separate from a proposed implementation. A user asking for greater movement has not necessarily asked for a new geometry representation.

Record the repository revision, worktree state and relevant model factory. Preserve unrelated edits, supplied artwork and previously published editions. The implementation documented here is pinned to 1e4ef518d6943ab1af39cef3b4d558f209a17891; a later working tree is a new baseline, not a reason to silently reinterpret the book. Before using a chapter's numeric value, check whether the active code still agrees.

Define allowed writes and output boundaries. A diagnostic capture does not authorize editing the application model to make the capture easier. A book request does not authorize publishing private ROMs, raw recordings or conversation history. A local verification does not imply permission to push or deploy. Follow the actual user's authority for those operations.

Inspect the existing numbered workstreams and contributor instructions. For this project's established workflow, retain the TODO index, numbered workstream, development ledger and all required status, purpose, task, acceptance, evidence and completion fields. Keep technical completion separate from aesthetic approval. Where remote tracking is authorized, verify the real issue and Project status rather than merely writing an issue URL into a local file.
Construct a model contract

Write a compact contract before changing geometry. It should identify the root group, local axes, scale convention, primary silhouette, geometry helpers, material roles, texture sources, movable subgroups, returned handles and disposal owner. Add the important interaction surfaces and collision envelopes. If any of those are unknown, make them a question to resolve in source or a small experiment; do not fill them with a plausible guess.

For a console, include the front/back convention, shell layers, seam, bezel opening, active display, inactive glass, buttons, grips, ports, labels and cartridge relation. For the DS, add the lower-deck origin, upper-lid pivot, hinge geometry, separate screens, stylus and touch coordinates. For a companion, include body shape, face projection, expression groups, limbs, light contribution, drag/rest states and full bounds.

Separate appearance from mechanism. An object can look rounded because of an actual bevel, a smooth normal field or a material response. Those are different constructions with different costs. A character can look soft because of the silhouette, curvature and diffuse material without a deformable physical simulation. A screen can look bright because it is unlit, emissive or externally illuminated; those mechanisms affect color and exposure differently.

Name dimensions by what they control. A parameter in radians is not a distance in model units. A local offset is not a world-space displacement after parent rotation. A physical lamp dimension in meters is not necessarily the scene unit used by the console. Carry units through the worked calculations and into diagnostic output.
Rebuild the hierarchy in a small scene

Instantiate the original factory in an isolated scene before reconstructing it manually. Load required image resources first. In particular, await loadBrand() before calling the GBA factory, because its canvas textures draw the shared brand image during construction. Do not treat an import as resource readiness.

Capture a front, rear and three-quarter view with a declared projection. Compute bounds from the complete hierarchy after updating world matrices. Fit the camera to all corners rather than a guessed center and radius that can crop a protruding limb or stylus. Make any pose override explicit. In this edition's atlas, the DS returned lid group receives a fifteen-degree local-X rotation; this is a diagnostic pose, not a public setHinge method or a claim about the application's play angle.

Use neutral lighting to understand base surfaces, then test the real application lighting separately. When disabling material emission or model lights, record that policy in the capture receipt and caption. Do not present a studio render as proof that the table lamp produces the same result in the application.

Inspect large masses before details. Compare silhouette width, height, recess placement and front/back thickness. Then inspect seams, bevels, controls and small markings. Rebuilding detail before establishing scale tends to produce local perfection attached to the wrong global proportions.

If a primitive is transformed, inspect its local axes before applying the parent transform. A cylinder's construction axis, an extruded shape's depth and a plane's normal can differ. The relevant chapter explains each usage; do not assume one helper's orientation is a repository-wide convention.
Preserve the visible surface

For layered hard-surface models, draw a cross-section on paper or in a small diagram. Identify which surface forms the recess floor, which forms the surrounding rim, which is an active display and which is glass. Check that the layers do not intersect, produce z-fighting or overwrite one another's intended color.

For facial patches on a curved body, apply the intended expression shape before projecting onto the shell. Translating already projected geometry can bury one end of the feature or detach it from the surface. The correct operation depends on the body's actual surface parameterization and the intended transform owner.

Test every movement extreme with every supported expression, not only a centered smile. Check the visibility of the foremost geometry from the real camera. A local visible property or a finite vertex coordinate does not establish that the eye or freckle is outside the body and visible to the user. Ancestor visibility and intervening geometry also matter.

Preserve the complete feature set when changing the gaze range. Tiny freckles and facial accents are easy to omit from an expression-only test while still being visibly wrong. Compare the projected screen-space displacement to the user's intended viewer-left, viewer-right, up or down direction; a world-axis sign alone does not establish that result after rotation.

Do not hide a surface problem with brighter emission or a different camera. Isolate geometry, normal orientation, material settings and illumination as separate variables. Restore the actual scene conditions before accepting the change.
Treat materials as separate contracts

Record which surfaces use lit physical/standard materials and which deliberately do not. Preserve the active LCD's color path separately from inactive reflective glass and the surrounding plastic. Nearest sampling and mipmap choices belong to the display contract, not to every texture on the model.

Color values, output color space, tone mapping and exposure have to agree. A material that is pleasant in a studio can become unreadably dark or white in the application. A companion's emissive surface can overwhelm its facial detail even when its point light is correctly positioned. Raising global exposure can fix one object while breaking every other object.

When tuning, hold most variables fixed. Start with the visible body and screen under the real camera, then isolate the lamp, companion emitters and ambient contribution. Compare the same pose before and after the change. Record what the experiment actually excludes; turning off one companion is not the same as turning off both.

Small labels need an explicit resolution and filtering policy. Check the canvas crop, alpha processing, physical size and distance to the camera. A high-resolution texture is not automatically readable if the mark is physically too small, tilted, occluded or washed out. Respect supplied artwork and distinguish it from newly generated labels.
Integrate movement without losing ownership

Separate authoring pose, interaction pose and settled desk pose. A factory's initial coordinates do not automatically become the safe home position after the scene places several objects together. A focus or inspection mode may temporarily move a console without authorizing the overwrite of its saved table pose.

Use the actual animation timestamp appropriate to the mechanism. A stale render timestamp, an arbitrary number of updates and a wall-clock delay can disagree with painted motion. For a fall or cartridge sequence, inspect the intermediate visible pose, not only the final state variable.

After changing shape or pose, re-evaluate the complete component envelope. A limb can extend beyond the body's current axis-aligned box; a rotated object can sweep through a larger envelope than its final orientation. Collision-free contact at one angle does not establish clearance throughout manipulation.

When choosing a home position, inspect deterministic ordering and tie behavior. An algorithm can be correct for one object order and fail when equally ranked objects are considered in the other order. Preserve existing tolerances and cache invalidation semantics unless the requirement specifically changes them.

Do not equate smooth animation with a physics simulation. The project includes explicit motion and settling mechanisms; explain the actual equations and state transitions used. If introducing a real physics engine, that is a substantial new dependency and behavior change requiring its own requirements, tests and resource budget.
Preserve input ownership

Find the complete path from pointer location to selected geometry and from that geometry to the interaction owner. Occlusion, invisible ancestors, controls, stylus, lamp clicks, console dragging and inspection can compete. A model change can affect picking even when it does not change the visual design.

Test representative rays through the new shape and through neighboring controls. A broad invisible hit target may improve one interaction while stealing another. A decorative mesh may need to be ignored for a particular action without becoming globally invisible. Keep the existing ownership rules explicit.

For DS touch, preserve the relationship among the screen geometry, its world transform and touch coordinates. A visual change to a curved screen or frame should not silently change the emulated touch domain. Inspect real coordinate conversion and the active surface, not an unrelated screenshot rectangle.
Use a layered validation plan

Start with the smallest deterministic checks that can reject the intended bug. For geometry, inspect component presence, dimensions, local relationships and finite values. For surface visibility, use actual foremost-hit or rendered evidence at the movement extremes. For interaction, exercise the correct pointer owner. For motion, inspect the painted intermediate and settled poses.

Add focused coverage only for the behavior introduced or fixed. Avoid tests that merely repeat constants or assert implementation spelling. Prefer a case that would fail on the old behavior and succeeds on the new visible outcome. Keep assertions meaningful when diagnosing environmental

Use the established bounded-recovery rule for application tests: one justified repair attempt, then explicitly park a repeatedly failing case with its assertions retained and coverage debt recorded. Do not add retries until a flaky test happens to pass, weaken an unrelated requirement or report a skip as a fixed behavior.

Broaden validation when shared construction helpers, transform ownership, render scheduling or input routing are affected. A small visual patch can have a wide dependency boundary. Conversely, do not rerun an unrelated full suite repeatedly after the relevant checks have passed and nothing has changed.

Record the exact revision and environment of a hosted run. A local browser result is not a hosted deployment result; a successful build is not gameplay verification; a screenshot is not an input test. Count declared, passed, skipped, failed and unrun cases separately, and inspect all required shards and the actual deployment job.
Reproduce the diagnostic atlas
Run the existing generator from the repository root in an environment with the locked application and production dependencies and an installed supported Chromium browser:

node docs\modeling-book\tools\capture-model-atlas.mjs
python docs\modeling-book\tools\make-atlas-plates.py --review $env:BOOK_REVIEW_DIR

Set BOOK_REVIEW_DIR to an explicitly chosen private review directory before the second command. It is an output location, not a source of model images. A missing value must be corrected, not replaced by a success-shaped empty image report.

The capture generator verifies the pinned first-party sources, records raw and committed hashes, blocks external requests and writes eighteen PNGs plus its manifest. The plate tool composes those captures into an original six-model cover and a contact sheet. It does not redraw geometry or synthesize a replacement model image.

Read the receipt and inspect the actual contact sheet. Check for cropped limbs, missing controls, wrong front/back labeling, invisible faces and incorrect lid pose. The expected mesh count establishes inventory continuity, not visual correctness by itself. A future intended geometry change requires a new source cutoff and an explicitly new atlas, not editing an old receipt.
Rebuild this book without touching the old editions
The modeling edition uses its own assembler and route:

node --test docs\book\production\production.test.mjs
python -B -m unittest discover -s docs\book\production -p native_rules_test.py
node docs\book\production\build-models.mjs
node docs\book\production\render.mjs --models

The default route belongs to the GBA book; --nds belongs to the NDS-only book. Do not use either to update this handbook. The three routes have separate candidate and output directories. Existing qualified PDFs and the NDS reader are preserved by exact hash checks.

The modeling assembler verifies source spans against cached immutable Git blobs, checks the four model-coverage receipts, enforces substantive per-chapter and total prose floors, and embeds approved metadata-clean illustrations. It rejects a repeated long paragraph rather than counting a copied passage as new substance. Code blocks, image markup and URLs do not satisfy the prose requirement.

The renderer lays out the actual manuscript, renders Mermaid diagrams and computes chapter page ranges. Both browser and native checks require at least two hundred real pages and two hundred unique chapter-content pages. Cover, contents, part/chapter openers and reference appendices do not supply those chapter-content pages. Typography is inherited from the readable shared print style; padding and oversized type are not a depth strategy.

The native reviewer checks searchable content coverage, chapter markers, A4 bounds, links, bookmarks, embedded fonts and private-path leakage. Its privacy expression distinguishes a real Windows drive from an ordinary HTTPS URL. The offline reader is tested without scripts or external requests. Those are specific mechanical qualifications, not proof that all wording is correct or every page has been visually reviewed.

Inspect the generated contact sheets and selected native pages. Record the exact inspected scope and PDF hash in the edition review. A rebuild invalidates an earlier visual-review note. Do not describe a thumbnail-level review as full-resolution inspection of every diagram.
Package and publish only what was authorized

Keep published byte-preservation attributes with the artifact checksums. On Windows, automatic line-ending conversion can change generated HTML or JSON between a qualified working file and its staged Git object. Verify the staged object bytes, not only the working tree, before declaring that the sealed edition will be delivered unchanged.

Stage an explicit allowlist. Exclude private inputs, raw captures not intended for publication, transient candidates, local review sheets, unrelated artwork and context stores. Keep the front README short and GIF-first; its role is to point to this book, not to absorb the book's construction explanations.

After an authorized push, verify the exact remote revision and actual downloaded artifact bytes. Monitor the exact deployment associated with that revision, including required browser shards, build and deployment jobs. A previous successful run cannot qualify a later commit.

Create or update only the owned MeshBoard persona when publishing the requested local reference thread. Use a professional-English question root, register the open thread, and add substantive replies with correct ownership and reply references. Verify the generated index and both thread views. A local board post is not an external social-network publication and does not wake another agent.
Leave a better handoff

End with the visible outcome, the meaningful mechanism changed, the exact source/artifact identity and any real limitation. Update public development evidence and private continuity for their separate audiences. Preserve prior history instead of rewriting a failed experiment into an uninterrupted success story.

For a future extension, leave a small reconstruction recipe: required inputs, coordinate assumptions, geometry sequence, material roles, hierarchy, interaction owner, relevant views, regression checks and disposal policy. If the technique came from researched guidance rather than the implementation, label it. If a statement remains unverified, say so plainly.

The new agent's advantage should be better evidence and a clearer method, not borrowed confidence. That is how this handbook can improve over time without pretending that one document contains every possible modeling decision.
Sources, model coverage and research limits
Immutable implementation, later manuscript

The public implementation cutoff for this handbook is 1e4ef518d6943ab1af39cef3b4d558f209a17891 in Zanark/BowserBoy. Chapter source links use that revision. The assembler checks each cited file and line range against the actual committed blob and caches repeated reads. It does not treat a successful HTTP response, a search-result preview or a matching filename as source verification.

The source manifest records the exact manuscript, production, atlas and coverage inputs used for the edition. Those later-created files are not retroactively placed at the implementation cutoff. Relative references to new supplementary files under this book may point to the living main branch; those links are recorded separately and are not immutable implementation evidence.

The relevant public entry points are the application dependency declaration, the handheld factory and geometry helpers, the DS factory, Pear Boy, the axolotl, the lamp and lighting systems, and scene integration. The chapters provide narrower line-level evidence and supporting motion, input and regression references.
Coverage is an explicit inventory

Part one covers the GBA's shell, seams, front/rear layers, recess, LCD, controls, grips, generated details, cartridges and texture/artwork boundaries. It explicitly distinguishes the curved LCD outline from a thick optical lens; no separate transmissive GBA glass slab exists at this cutoff. Its foundation chapters explain the library, reference and geometry contracts needed to reconstruct those objects.

Part two covers the DS lower deck, upper lid, hinge-related construction, hardware, controls, markings, separate planar displays, reflective powered-off glass material, stylus, touch domain, cartridge choreography, inspection and model regression evidence. Curved DS cover geometry is a labeled extension proposal, not an implemented model. The stylus and cartridge are not omitted merely because they are subordinate objects rather than independent top-level factories.

Part three covers Pear Boy's body and face, projection, expressions, gaze, freckles, limbs and rope, plus the axolotl's body, gills, tail and facial features. It then connects the companions to light emission, dragging, gravity, settling and complete clearance envelopes.

Part four covers the desk, room, tripod lamp and shared systems that make every model behave coherently: exposure, color, shadows, reflections, screen materials, picking, render lifecycle, algorithms, design principles, bounded recovery and causal history.

The four coverage/part-*.json files retain per-model source, symbol, component, chapter, test and limitation records. They also list actual source reads, consulted research and historical evidence. The assembler checks their structure and basic family coverage. That mechanical inventory is not
a semantic proof that every code line or visual nuance has a correct explanation; the chapter review and explicit limitations remain necessary.

An empty mapped-test list explicitly means no mapped test, never a pass. Installed dependency metadata and this later manuscript are recorded separately from files that exist at the implementation cutoff.
Libraries and asset provenance

The application models are constructed procedurally with Three.js; browser canvas code creates many textures and markings. Playwright is a browser-automation dependency, not the mesh-authoring library. The book pipeline separately uses Markdown-it, Mermaid, Paged.js, Playwright Core, PyMuPDF and Pillow. Do not merge those roles into a claim that a PDF tool built the handheld geometry.

Version declarations, lockfiles, installed-package identities and actual served resource hashes answer different questions. Chapter one explains the application toolchain; the edition manifest identifies production inputs; the atlas receipt records the actual browser and Three package used for the captures. A lockfile alone does not establish that an arbitrary installed directory is intact.

The factories use existing supplied brand artwork as well as generated labels. The atlas and cover are original diagnostic compositions of the project's actual procedural geometry, not photographs, historical design drawings or AI-generated replacements. The capture manifest describes lighting, pose, projection, source identity and limitations. The project's third-party notices remain part of the delivered edition.

No commercial ROM, firmware, private game recording or raw conversation is required to reconstruct the illustrated models. The atlas deliberately leaves factory displays in their non-gameplay state. Existing authorized application demonstrations, when referenced in the living documentation, have their own media provenance and do not become proof of every mechanism discussed here.
External research is bounded

Each part's coverage receipt records consulted external references, consultation date, supported mechanism and scope. Chapter citations explain the specific use. Official library or browser documentation is used to clarify geometry, transforms, materials, rendering and platform behavior, not to invent an original modeling history.

Current documentation may have changed since the pinned implementation or may describe a different release. Verify version-specific behavior against the installed package and the relevant code before applying a recommendation. If a chapter proposes an alternative, it is not evidence that the alternative is already deployed.

Short explanatory code and equations are teaching tools unless explicitly identified as exact source. Preserve actual source attribution, and do not confuse a reduced worked example with a complete drop-in replacement for a factory.
Verification and non-claims

The production manifest records actual chapter prose counts, diagrams, learning markers, illustration derivatives, implementation source hashes, atlas policy and preservation checks. The browser layout report and native PDF review identify actual pages, chapter ranges, text coverage, links, fonts and bounds. The checksum file identifies delivered bytes.

The edition's review note states the actual visual inspection performed for that exact PDF. Generated review images are candidates for inspection, not proof that inspection occurred. Mechanical success does not imply human acceptance, independent rights clearance, PDF/UA accessibility, printer prepress, a fresh-machine rebuild or byte-for-byte reproduction across browsers.

The modeling edition guards the earlier GBA PDF, NDS PDF and NDS offline reader without rebuilding them. Their preservation is not new validation of the old application or repair of previously parked browser cases. Any application CI accounting must name the actual revision and run and keep passed, skipped, failed and unrun counts separate.

This book aims to make modeling decisions reconstructable, but it is not a literal replica of an assistant and cannot guarantee complete transfer of undocumented knowledge. Improvements should add source-backed mechanisms, experiments and corrected limitations rather than confident filler. When evidence ends, the claim ends with it.

How to use this reconstruction manual

This book explains how BowserBOY's first-party three-dimensional objects are constructed, assembled, animated and verified. Its central subject is not the emulator instruction set. It is the deceptively large amount of geometry and engineering required to make a small handheld console, a second articulated console, two expressive companions and a believable desk behave as one coherent interactive world.

The purpose is transfer. A future agent should be able to inspect the implementation, identify the mechanism behind a visible detail, reconstruct that mechanism in a small experiment, and extend it without relying on this conversation. The book therefore keeps exact source references, parameter meanings, worked calculations, changed-condition retries and explained exercises beside the construction discussion. It does not claim to copy a model's hidden reasoning, transfer every previous memory or guarantee that a different agent will make identical artistic judgments.
What belongs to this edition

The implementation cutoff is 1e4ef518d6943ab1af39cef3b4d558f209a17891 in the public Zanark/BowserBoy repository. A cutoff makes the teaching inspectable: a later improvement must not silently become evidence for an earlier explanation. The manuscript, diagnostic atlas and publishing tools were created after that implementation revision. Their exact input hashes belong to the edition manifests, rather than being misrepresented as files already present at the cutoff.

There are four parts. The first establishes libraries, references, coordinates, reusable geometry, the Game Boy Advance shell and its small physical details. The second follows the Nintendo DS from lower deck to articulated lid, dual display, stylus, controls and cartridge loading. The third constructs Pear Boy and the axolotl, including curved face projection, expressions, soft-looking surfaces, movement and clearance. The fourth explains the supporting desk, room, tripod lamp, rendering, input ownership, performance, algorithms, design principles, regression evidence and historical changes.

The desk and wall are not incidental background. A convincing tabletop controls apparent contact, scale, shadow direction and whether a moved object seems to float. A lamp is not only a mesh: the visible shade, world-space emitter, exposure and shadow policy have to agree. A face is not only a set of eyes: its features have to remain outside the actual body surface as it follows the pointer. Those connections are part of modeling, not unrelated implementation detail.

This is a third, independent book. The existing GBA engineering book and the separate NDS development-journey book remain useful references and are not overwritten. This handbook deliberately includes both console families and their common systems because the subject is the complete modeling workflow. It does not import the GBA chapters into the NDS-only book.
Read the evidence labels literally
Four classes of statements occur throughout the chapters.

Implemented behavior describes source at the pinned revision. The strongest references identify the file, the relevant symbol or section, and actual line ranges. A source reference can establish what a constructor creates or what an update function calculates. It cannot by itself prove what a particular browser visibly displayed.

Historical evidence describes a change supported by a commit, tracked workstream or existing regression record. A development history reconstructed from those records is not a verbatim transcript of an author's thoughts. A later test name is not proof that the test existed when an earlier shape was first modeled.

Researched guidance comes from an identified external reference, such as Three.js or a browser-platform reference. Documentation consulted later can explain a general mechanism or suggest a better experiment. It does not retroactively prove the project's original intent, and a current documentation page need not describe every detail of the installed library version.

Proposed extensions are recommendations. A proposed optimization, alternate modeling tool or broader test matrix is not already implemented because it appears in a textbook. Carry that distinction into future changes and into their completion reports.

Hash equality is also a narrow claim. It can establish the identity of a file, an illustration or an artifact. It does not establish semantic correctness, aesthetic approval, reproducibility on an untested machine or the rights to redistribute a third-party work. The native PDF and browser checks make specific assertions about content, dimensions, links and layout; they are not an all-purpose certificate.
Follow a model through five layers

For each object, begin with its silhouette. If a reader cannot recognize the console or companion from an uncluttered three-quarter view, tiny labels will not rescue the design. Reconstruct the main masses first, establish an origin and local axes, then add recesses, controls and markings.

Next, inspect the surface construction. A pale silicone body, painted shell, rubber pad, LCD and glass overlay should not be treated as interchangeable material presets. Ask which geometry owns the visible contour, which material receives light, which surface is unlit by design and which layer exists only to provide a reflection.

Then identify the transform owner. A DS lid rotates around a hinge-related local origin; a whole console moves through another group; a companion's gaze can move its facial features without dragging its entire body. An attractive pose in one hierarchy is not evidence that the hierarchy remains correct when a parent rotates.

The fourth layer is interaction. A button can be visually present but geometrically occluded. A face can report a visible flag yet be buried beneath another surface. A lamp can remain in the correct pose while its effective light position fails to follow. Inspect the world-space result and the foremost rendered surface, not only a convenient state field.

Finally, examine lifecycle and regression evidence. A model factory allocates buffers, materials and textures. A render loop decides when motion is sampled and when shadows or reflections are refreshed. A change to a limb can enlarge a collision envelope even if its resting pose looks unchanged. Modeling precision therefore includes resource ownership, animation timing and clearance.
The atlas is a controlled experiment

The illustrations in assets/atlas are fresh renders of the actual procedural factory geometry. There are front, back and three-quarter orthographic views of the GBA, DS, Pear Boy, axolotl, tripod lamp and cartridge. The original factory code was not edited to make the images.

The capture environment intentionally differs from the application. It uses a neutral studio background, separate studio lights, ACES tone mapping at exposure one and an orthographic camera fitted to each complete model. Factory light objects are hidden and material emission is disabled so that base surfaces remain inspectable. The DS's returned lid group is rotated fifteen degrees around local X for a readable diagnostic open pose. The application sets its own poses, lighting and exposure.

Those conditions matter. A pale companion in the atlas is not a demonstration of its powered lamp appearance. The captured GBA's white display is its factory material, not proof of game execution. A visible model edge is useful construction evidence; it does not demonstrate a shadow produced by the table lamp in the real room. Captions and the capture manifest retain these limits.

The generator loads the shared brand images before constructing the GBA. Its canvas textures use decoded image data immediately; simply importing a constructor is insufficient. The loopback server serves only approved module and image resources, and the browser blocks external requests. No ROM, firmware, native emulator startup or private recording is needed to reproduce these illustrations.

The source identity check distinguishes Windows line endings from substantive edits. It compares pinned and working source after explicit CRLF-to-LF normalization, while recording the raw capture-input hashes separately. Do not report those two identities as byte equality. The manifest also records actual served resource hashes, browser version, model bounds and mesh counts.
Figure O.1. The original six-model cover plate is composed from actual three-quarter captures. It compares shapes, not physical scale between objects or application-room lighting.
Use the learning structure

Every chapter has a stable MDxx identity. A W section is a worked example: follow the concrete setup and explain why the result follows. An R section changes a condition and requires a new decision rather than copying the previous answer. A Q section presents an exercise; its paired A section explains the reasoning and the failure modes, not just a final number.

When adapting a technique, write down the invariant before changing the code. For a face, an invariant might concern surface clearance and visibility across all expressions. For a console, it might concern the relation between the bezel opening, active screen and glass. For a movable companion, it includes the complete component envelope and a collision-free settled pose.

Use the exercises to find a misunderstanding before making a broad patch. If the proposed change cannot be explained in local coordinates, isolate a small model and draw the parent-child relationship. If a lighting adjustment cannot distinguish material emission from external illumination, test those contributions separately. A short controlled experiment is more useful than repeatedly tuning several unrelated constants.
Reconstruct before you generalize

The shortest route through the book for a new agent is foundations, the model family being changed, algorithms, design principles and reconstruction. Read the neighboring interaction and lifecycle chapters before changing a shape that is animated or draggable. The book's source inventory and standalone handoff help locate those boundaries, but neither substitutes for reading the relevant implementation.

Reproduce the existing behavior first. Establish the baseline silhouette, dimensions, material roles, transform hierarchy and a few representative views. Save the exact source revision and capture conditions. Only then change one construction layer and evaluate the result. Otherwise a new lighting setup can disguise a bad normal, a different camera can hide an intersection and a broad refactor can make the cause of an improvement impossible to identify.

Do not install an alternative authoring tool merely because it appears in a researched recommendation. The established application constructs its models procedurally with Three.js and browser canvas textures. An external mesh editor can be a reasonable future choice, but it introduces a different source-of-truth, export, scale, normal, texture and licensing contract. It is a design decision, not a missing step that this book quietly assumes.

For reproducible commands, start in the repository root. The publishing and atlas recipes use the existing Node dependencies, Python image/PDF tools and an installed supported Chromium browser. Restore a missing dependency only when the chosen validation reports it missing, or when changing its manifest. The documented local qualification does not claim a fresh-machine setup or cross-platform test run.
Know when the work is actually done

A successful modeling change has several different outcomes. The intended geometry exists. The intended effect is visible from the relevant views. Interaction still selects the correct surface. Motion and clearance remain valid. Relevant regressions pass or an explicitly recorded limitation remains. Documentation explains the change without exporting private inputs.

A successful book has its own separate outcomes. The assembly contains the intended chapters and illustrations; real chapter prose is not replaced by code dumps; the printed PDF contains at least two hundred pages and at least two hundred unique chapter-content pages; links and learning markers survive native export; and the standalone reader opens without scripts or network dependencies. Cover, contents, part openers, chapter openers and appendices do not satisfy the content-page minimum.

Mechanical results, bounded visual inspection, user acceptance and publication are distinct. Read the exact edition's review note. Do not turn a generated contact sheet into a claim that every figure was inspected at full size, a deployment badge into a gameplay test, or a previous edition's review into approval of new bytes.

The transferable method is a sequence of evidence-backed decisions, not a list of magical parameter values. Preserve that sequence when improving the project, and the next agent will inherit a usable engineering manual instead of another long document that still requires the original conversation.

MD01 / EVIDENCE, LIBRARIES AND THE ACTUAL TOOLCHAIN
Evidence, libraries and the actual toolchain
What this reconstruction can establish

A useful modeling book must explain how to rebuild an object, not merely identify the library that draws it. This part reconstructs the Game Boy Advance family from executable geometry, image-processing operations, materials, tests, and recorded changes. Its implementation baseline is commit 1e4ef518d6943ab1af39cef3b4d558f209a17891. Numbers described as implementation values belong to that baseline. Exercises and proposed diagnostics are teaching additions, not claims that the original author used those procedures.

The central evidence is unusually direct: createHandheld() creates a group and populates it with named meshes; createCartridge() creates a second group; createWood() paints a texture. These are construction programs rather than imported finished models. Reading them reveals shapes, coordinate relationships, material sharing, and initial visibility. It does not reveal the author's unrecorded reasoning, physical measurements, or subjective approval. See the factory boundaries (src/handheld.js:392) and the cartridge and wood factories (src/handheld.js:645).

Use three evidence categories throughout this part. Implementation means behavior visible in the pinned source. Historical record means a commit diff or public workstream says something happened; that statement retains its date and limitations. Recommendation means a reproducible technique proposed here. These categories prevent a common documentation error: converting a sensible present-day workflow into an invented account of how a model was originally made.
The small runtime toolchain

The root manifest declares one runtime npm dependency, Three.js 0.186.1, and the development dependency @playwright/test 1.64.1. It declares ES modules and Node >=22. The lock entries and installed package manifests inspected for this reconstruction agree with those two versions. Agreement verifies this workspace's declarations and installation; it is not evidence that a clean machine was installed or tested during this writing. Manifest (package.json:1); locked packages (package-lock.json:20).

Three.js provides the scene graph, shapes, triangulation, extrusions, lathe geometry, materials, and textures used by these factories. Browser Canvas 2D supplies text rasterization and image processing. Neither a Blender project nor a GLTF loader participates in the construction path examined here. This is a bounded claim about these sources, not a claim that no external creative tool ever existed. In particular, supplied brand artwork is an input asset whose earlier creation cannot be reconstructed from the geometry factory.

The browser resolves the bare module name three through an import map to ./vendor/three.module.js. This is not a bundler rewriting application imports. The build copies allowlisted public files, including the Three module, core, light helpers, and license. Its separate demo-generation calls do not turn cartridge props into ROM-derived meshes. Browser entry (web/index.html:8); delivery map (scripts/site-files.mjs:4).
Figure MD01.1. The application resolves a packaged library into procedural factories; the delivery step does not author geometry.
Separate construction, presentation, and publishing

The book-production directory has its own manifest. Its Markdown parser, Mermaid, Paged.js, and browser automation dependencies produce documentation, not the handheld. Sharing a package family or version between production and tests does not merge their responsibilities. When recording a toolchain, assign each dependency to the operation it actually performs; otherwise a future agent might look for a CAD export that never existed. Production manifest (docs/book/production/package.json:1).

Similarly, a diagnostic render is a presentation of factory output. It can expose topology, layering, silhouette, or missing assets under controlled light. It cannot prove the room's final lighting behavior, emulator upload cadence, or accessible interaction. Those require integration evidence. The browser test that raycasts the LCD, speaker slot, and D-pad well is stronger evidence of those particular surfaces than a flattering front image, but it does not establish an accurate physical replica.

The historical record supports this distinction. The initial tabletop workstream records an actual-mesh requirement and later records rejection of the first shape despite passing tests. The reference correction explicitly separates independent geometry from extraction of a supplied reference model. Those records teach why visual and technical acceptance are different, without granting either one today. Recorded correction (TODO/07_REFERENCE_SHAPE.todo:18).
MD01-W01 Trace one visible object to its dependencies

Consider the A button. Begin at the named A button mesh, not a screenshot. The factory uses a lathed cap, selects a cloned rubber material, and attaches recessed lettering. The letter outline is recovered from browser-rendered Arial alpha; contour extraction turns that raster boundary into geometry. Thus the button depends on Three.js and browser text rasterization even though its final letter is not a painted decal. The distinction matters when comparing machines: the system font can affect a geometric cut.

Next identify dependencies that do not belong to that object. The loaded cartridge's title canvas does not determine the A glyph. The book renderer does not determine the lathe profile. The native emulator shader does not manufacture the cap. A rigorous receipt names these negative boundaries only after following the positive construction chain. Cap and glyph construction (src/handheld.js:116); glyph recovery (src/handheld.js:232).

The following original diagnostic is runnable in the browser developer console of an already-served project page. It does not load a ROM, call the complete handheld factory, or change the application. It creates a separate cartridge and reports its structural receipt. Its assumptions are a functioning page import map and browser Canvas 2D. Expected outcomes are five named grip meshes and two text planes, not a pixel-identical image across all operating systems.

Why inspect the object without rendering it? It isolates factory assembly from camera, lighting, and the live scene's state. A missing grip count is a construction problem. A present grip that cannot be seen in a render may instead be behind another surface or below image resolution. This staged distinction reduces speculative parameter editing.
MD01-R01 Retry when the library appears correct but imports fail

Suppose the installed package version is correct, yet the browser reports that three cannot be resolved. Reinstalling packages is not the first justified repair. Check whether the served HTML contains the import map, whether its relative vendor URL resolves under the current base path, and whether both module and core files were delivered. The build maps source locations to public destinations; a filesystem import that works in Node does not demonstrate browser delivery.

Now change the condition: the import succeeds, but createHandheld() fails while drawing the wordmark. This is a different boundary. brandImage is a live export populated by asynchronous image loading. The factory draws it directly. The relevant repair investigation is initialization order and asset decoding, not Three.js geometry segmentation. Brand loader (src/brand.js:1).

Record each retry with its changed condition and observable result. “Dependencies fixed” is too broad. “Vendor module now resolves; brand image still undecoded” preserves useful causal information. It also avoids claiming clean-machine reproduction merely because a warm workspace recovered. A future agent should be able to repeat the narrow observation without inheriting an unexplained success label.
Figure MD01.2. Diagnose the earliest failed boundary before changing a later modeling parameter.
MD01-Q01 Decide what a successful test proves

An agent reports: “The real-3D browser case passed, so the GBA is dimensionally accurate, the source model was imported legally, every control remains illuminated while pressed, and the book is ready to publish.” Identify which parts follow from the inspected evidence. Design a stronger replacement report without running a publishing operation.
MD01-A01 Evidence has a measurable scope

The report overreaches in four different directions. The real-3D case checks a triangle threshold, movement into play, front orientation, particular raycast surfaces, and further interaction behavior. Its surface assertions establish an unobstructed center LCD, a recessed speaker comparison, and a bounded pivot well. They do not compare a caliper measurement or CAD reference. Replace “dimensionally accurate” with those explicit observations. Surface assertions (tests/browser/scene.spec.mjs:1351).

The reference workstream says the geometry was independently authored and the external model was unavailable for extraction. That is a historical provenance statement, not a license grant discovered by a geometry test. The complete-press-response test is explicitly parked in the pinned suite, while separate aperture-lighting cases contain active assertions. Their existence cannot be summarized as a fresh pass of all controls under every light. Publication readiness requires its own authorized integration process; neither a mesh test nor this chapter performs it.

A defensible replacement report identifies the pinned revision, exact inspected or executed cases, active versus skipped status, and unmeasured properties. This writing inspected tests but did not execute them. That limitation is useful rather than embarrassing: it tells the next agent precisely where new evidence is required.
Research that informs recommendations, not history
Build a receipt that another agent can challenge

A useful reconstruction receipt has an input identity, an operation, an observation, and a limitation. For example, identify the pinned handheld factory, describe creating an independent cartridge, report five grip meshes, and state that no rendering or runtime insertion was exercised. A later agent can challenge any one of these elements without discarding the whole account. “Looks correct” has no comparable structure.

Line citations serve a related purpose. Cite the helper that defines a bevel convention as well as the call site that chooses a particular bevel. Citing only the call site leaves readers guessing whether the geometry is centered or how thickness expands. Citing only the helper cannot prove that the shell actually uses it. The source pair creates a short, auditable construction chain.

For version-sensitive recommendations, record the gap between what documentation describes and what the implementation invokes. A current API page can contain features added after the project was pinned. It is not safe to retrofit those features into the historical account simply because they would simplify the explanation. Prefer the subset confirmed by the source, then label newer alternatives explicitly.

Finally, preserve failures and skipped checks as first-class evidence. An unresolved retained-frame reload issue belongs beside the otherwise useful CRT assertions, not in an unrelated footnote. An unavailable font is an input limitation, not an excuse to claim exact contours anyway. This approach makes a book useful as an engineering handoff: the next agent receives both a construction method and the edges beyond which it must gather new evidence.

The current Three.js Object3D documentation, BufferGeometry documentation, and CanvasTexture documentation were consulted on 2026-11-07. They support teaching about local/world transforms, indexed attributes and normals, and canvas-backed textures. They are latest documentation, not a frozen description of the project's original development environment. The implementation and lockfile remain authoritative for what this project actually calls and installs.
PART 1 / FOUNDATIONS AND THE GAME BOY ADVANCE
The modeling contract and visual references
Inspect the shape. Reconstruct the mechanism. Verify the visible result.
MD02 / THE MODELING CONTRACT AND VISUAL REFERENCES
The modeling contract and visual references
A reference is a question, not a mesh specification

The hardest modeling decision often precedes the first vertex: deciding what the object must communicate. Here the historical reference correction names a stepped upper crown, straighter sides, outward lower bow, lower-profile controls, and an angled recessed grille. These are actionable shape relationships. “Make it look more like a GBA” is not. The record also says the first model was rejected despite technical test success. Treat that as a warning against letting a passing runtime suite define aesthetic correctness. Reference contract (TODO/07_REFERENCE_SHAPE.todo:1).

This chapter reconstructs a contract from public artifacts; it does not recover the author's thoughts. The external reference's recorded download and license availability are historical observations, not a current audit of that service. The implemented model remains a set of independently specified curves and primitives. No dimensional drawing, calibrated photograph, or measurement survey is present in the evidence read for this part. Consequently, source units must remain scene units, not retroactively invented millimeters.

Begin with observable relationships: the crown is narrower than the widest side region; the screen sits centrally; the D-pad and action buttons occupy opposite sides; the speaker slots descend on the right; the rear has a separate battery cover. Each relationship can be traced to source coordinates. None requires reproducing copyrighted reference artwork. This distinction makes the workflow reusable: analyze organization and silhouette, then author original geometry whose parameters and limitations are explicit.
Translate appearance into layers of obligation

A useful contract has four layers. Identity asks whether the outline and landmark arrangement read as the intended device. Construction asks whether holes, floors, relief, and depth ordering actually exist. Behavior asks whether the assembled hierarchy can move and be inspected without separating parts. Evidence asks how each previous claim will be observed. Keeping these layers separate prevents an easy screenshot from becoming the only acceptance test.

The implementation provides a concrete identity scaffold. The outline reaches the central crown at y=2.42, uses side control points around x=±4.28, and bows downward through a control point at y=-2.61. These are path controls, not guaranteed final extrema. Extrusion bevels also expand the eventual surface. A bounding-box test must measure the generated geometry rather than substitute the largest literal found in the path. Outline construction (src/handheld.js:410).

Construction obligations are more specific. The thin front face receives control and speaker holes; recessed dark surfaces lie behind those openings. A mark intended to be molded uses geometry, while the bezel wordmark uses a processed texture. Behavior obligations preserve cap-child lettering and the loaded cartridge's parent relationship. These distinctions are not cosmetic bookkeeping: they decide which transformations and materials should change together.
Figure MD02.1. A reference becomes useful when translated into independent parameters and bounded observations.
Choose landmarks before choosing detail density

Landmarks make comparisons interpretable. For this device, use the crown center, shoulder transitions, widest sides, bottom bow, screen center, control centers, and battery cover. Compare these before screw slots or chrome tint. A beautiful screw cannot repair an oval silhouette that violates the reference contract. This is a recommended analysis order, not a claim that the original implementation was written in this sequence.

The source's control table is especially valuable because it separates functional locations from visual commentary. A is at (3.55,.50), B at (2.76,-.02), Start at (-2.64,-.98), and Select at (-2.70,-1.5). Their socket radii differ from cap radii. That gives two independent checks: landmark position and local clearance. The D-pad opening is constructed from a scaled cross rather than a circular placeholder. Control landmarks (src/handheld.js:434).

Assets need their own contract. The brand loader decodes four supplied PNGs, whereas the factory derives a wordmark from brandImage. An independently modeled shell does not imply independently authored input artwork. Conversely, supplied artwork does not mean the shell came from an imported model. Document these ownership boundaries separately so a future agent does not confuse provenance of pixels with provenance of triangles. Asset inputs (src/brand.js:1).
MD02-W01 Derive a measurable speaker requirement

Suppose a reference review says “the grille should be recessed, not raised rails.” Translate that sentence into a surface experiment. First select a point near a slot center, (3.02,-.79). Then select the neighboring solid face at (3.02,-.87). Shoot both rays from the front along the device's negative local Z direction. Convert both hit positions back into root-local coordinates and subtract their depths. A positive face-minus-slot result shows a recession at these sample locations.

The existing browser case does exactly this kind of comparison and requires a difference above .02 scene units. It is not a measurement of every point in all six slots. It does, however, reject a surface arrangement where both probes land on a raised decorative strip. Existing sample and threshold (tests/browser/scene.spec.mjs:1370).
An original pseudocode recipe extends the reasoning without pretending to be an existing test:

Pedagogical recipe; use a factory root with fresh matrices.
For each of six speaker slots:
  Raycast the center from local positive Z.
  Raycast a neighboring solid-face point.
  Convert both hits into root-local coordinates.
  Record faceZ minus slotZ and both mesh names.
Expect every chosen center to hit a lower receiving surface.
Reject missing hits; do not convert them into zero depth.

This recipe assumes the neighboring point really lies between slots, not inside a rotated aperture. The slots are angled .23 radians, so a naive vertical offset can become ambiguous near their ends. Begin at the shared X center where the original comparison is understood, then derive offset points in the slot's local frame if broadening coverage. The experiment is geometric; it does not prove the opening looks good under every material or light.

Now connect the requirement to construction. The face receives a rounded hole path; the dark grille is a separate shape behind it. If the ray hits an underlying shell instead of the named grille, the depth result may still be positive. Recording hit names prevents silently accepting the wrong ownership. This is why a good modeling contract specifies both shape and observable component identity.
MD02-R01 Retry when a closer view changes the judgment

Imagine the front diagnostic looks convincing at thumbnail scale, but an oblique close-up makes the controls appear pasted on. Do not immediately increase bevel segments. First ask which obligation failed: missing cap curvature, missing socket clearance, floating marks, or wrong material response? The source uses a lathed cap and genuine A/B cutouts, so a current failure might instead arise from view angle, an altered transform, or loss of the intended floor depth.

Change one condition at a time. Hold the model pose and replace decorative lighting with neutral studio light for shape diagnosis. Then hold light and rotate to inspect depth. Finally restore the room to check presentation. The parent-provided atlas images in this book are diagnostic factory renders under neutral lighting; they are not historical screenshots or evidence of live-room behavior. That limitation is the reason for using them, not an apology for them.

The old geometry chapter records successive changes from raised markings through recessed shapes to recovered Arial contours. It demonstrates that “softer” can refer to color, outline, or shadow depth. A retry should therefore name the changed property explicitly. “Reduced groove depth while preserving contour and cap material” is reproducible; “made letters nicer” is not. Historical distinctions (docs/book/chapters/04-handheld-geometry/README.md:39).
Figure MD02.2. Separate shape, material, and presentation hypotheses before deciding which parameter to change.
Precision without false metrology

Precision means controlling a defined quantity. It does not require pretending scene units are physical dimensions. A raycast depth comparison is precise in the model's coordinate system. A shortest-distance screen-edge fit is precise in sampled framebuffer pixels. A claim of hardware accuracy needs additional calibrated evidence that these sources do not supply. Keep the unit beside every threshold and explain the sample domain.

The LCD workstream is a useful precedent: it requires sampled image edges inside the geometry and a thin keyline, but explicitly calls the outline a fit rather than a guarantee for arbitrary shaders. Similarly, the player test changes native presets and checks that only CRT Geom uses curved geometry. That contract is conditional on the selected presentation, not an absolute requirement that every screen corner always be curved. LCD acceptance (TODO/13_CURVED_LCD_BORDER.todo:17); preset distinction (tests/browser/player.spec.mjs:265).
Choose comparisons that survive camera changes

A front silhouette comparison should use the device frame rather than the screen's current pixel rectangle. Perspective changes apparent spacing: a nearer shoulder can look wider without any geometry change. For a proposed parameter study, hold the camera fixed or compare orthographic diagnostic views, then use an oblique view to expose depth. This is a recommended experimental design, not a statement that the historical reference was calibrated.

Likewise, normalize a landmark comparison deliberately. Dividing every horizontal distance by shell width is useful for proportion, but it can hide an absolute clearance loss when the shell changes size. Record both the raw scene-unit gap and its normalized ratio. If the screen stays fixed while the case widens, these two quantities answer different questions: available space versus visual balance.

Do not treat every reference feature as mandatory. Some details may be occluded, licensed only for viewing, or ambiguous in perspective. Place those in an uncertainty list and author a bounded approximation instead of inventing unseen structure. That discipline is especially important for the simplified cartridge rear, whose absence of connector geometry is known from the factory rather than solved by imaginative reconstruction.
MD02-Q01 Define a contract for a wider handheld

A future agent proposes widening the shell by ten percent while leaving the screen unchanged. What observations should be required before accepting the change? Distinguish a visual redesign from faithful reconstruction, and explain why simply scaling the root is not the same experiment.
MD02-A01 Preserve the distinction between redesign and reconstruction

A wider shell is a proposed extension unless new evidence establishes it belongs to the pinned design. Record it as such. Keeping the LCD unchanged means root scaling is unsuitable: root scaling also widens the screen, changes control spacing, stretches text, and alters all child geometry. Instead define which shell path coordinates change and which landmarks remain fixed. Then regenerate or reposition dependent openings deliberately rather than let them drift as an accidental side effect.

Acceptance should compare front and oblique silhouettes, distances from controls to shell edges, speaker clearance, shoulder alignment, and actual LCD visibility. It should also inspect rear cover placement and screw locations, because a wider front with an unchanged rear can look assembled from unrelated parts. Interaction targets need fresh projection checks in the host, although those runtime changes lie beyond this part's factory analysis.

The answer is not “all tests pass.” Existing tests sample the old arrangement and may miss a new collision. Derive new probe points from the changed geometry, preserve the original baseline as a separate specimen, and report which observations are source-grounded versus proposed. That is how a modeling contract supports future agents without falsely freezing every aesthetic decision into universal truth.
